skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Access NCBI GEO datasets for gene expression and genomics research, including GSE, GSM, GPL, SOFT, Matrix, and GEOparse workflows.
skill.summary: Search, retrieve, download, and analyze NCBI GEO gene expression datasets.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation and examples for accessing public NCBI GEO data. I confirmed the plaintext FTP guidance as a medium concern because it can expose downloads to tampering. The remaining static findings are false positives involving public URLs, Markdown fences, placeholder keys, local data saves, and GEO identifiers.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS download URLs where available, or add checksum and provenance verification for files downloaded over FTP.

remediation.issue: API key shown as a literal assignment
remediation.suggestion: Show reading the NCBI API key from an environment variable or secret manager instead of a source-code string.

remediation.issue: Large local downloads and file writes
remediation.suggestion: Document destination directory validation, disk-space checks, and cache cleanup before bulk GEO downloads.

content.value_statement: Researchers often need reliable ways to find and reuse public gene expression datasets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through NCBI GEO search, retrieval, parsing, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles by keyword, organism, platform, disease, author, or study type.
Retrieve GEO metadata with Biopython Entrez E-utilities, including summaries and full records.
Download and parse GEO Series, Sample, and Platform records using GEOparse examples.
Explain SOFT, MINiML, series matrix, and supplementary file formats used by GEO.
Build expression matrices, inspect sample metadata, and outline basic quality control steps.
Support batch processing, metadata summaries, and simple cross-study expression comparisons.
limitations: It depends on NCBI availability, internet access, and current GEO file formats.
Large GEO files may require substantial storage, memory, and download time.
It does not validate biological conclusions or replace statistical review by a domain expert.
Examples require users to install and maintain Python packages such as GEOparse and Biopython.

use_cases.title: Find disease expression studies
use_cases.description: Search GEO for human disease datasets and summarize candidate GSE records for review.

use_cases.title: Prepare expression matrices
use_cases.description: Download a GEO Series, inspect sample metadata, and extract a matrix for downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Compare studies for a gene
use_cases.description: Locate platform probes for a gene and compare expression summaries across selected studies.

prompt_templates.title: Search for datasets
prompt_templates.prompt: Find NCBI GEO datasets about [condition] in [organism]. Return likely GSE accessions, study types, sample counts, and why each result is relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve study metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GEO guidance to review [GSE accession]. Summarize the title, organism, platform, samples, experimental design, and available file types.

prompt_templates.title: Plan expression analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow for downloading [GSE accession], extracting the expression matrix, separating control and treatment samples, and checking data quality.

prompt_templates.title: Design a meta-analysis workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reproducible GEO meta-analysis for [gene or pathway] across [GSE accessions]. Include metadata harmonization, probe mapping, normalization checks, and statistical cautions.

output_examples.input: Find GEO studies for breast cancer RNA-seq in humans.
output_examples.output: A concise shortlist of candidate GEO Series, with organism, technology, sample context, and next steps for metadata review.

output_examples.input: Explain what files I should download for GSE123456.
output_examples.output: A plain-language comparison of series matrix, SOFT, MINiML, and supplementary files, with guidance on when each format is useful.

output_examples.input: Plan a differential expression workflow for one GEO Series.
output_examples.output: A stepwise analysis plan covering download, metadata checks, group assignment, expression extraction, quality control, testing, and citation notes.

best_practices: Set an Entrez email address and respect NCBI rate limits for every automated query.
Check sample metadata, platform annotation, and processing methods before comparing expression values.
Cache large downloads locally and record dataset accessions, versions, and citations.
anti_patterns: Do not assume all GEO studies use comparable normalization or experimental design.
Do not download large supplementary files without checking disk space and file purpose.
Do not treat probe identifiers as gene symbols without platform-specific annotation mapping.

faq.question: What is NCBI GEO?
faq.answer: NCBI GEO is a public repository for gene expression and functional genomics datasets.

faq.question: Can this skill download GEO files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflows for GEOparse, E-utilities, and direct file downloads from GEO locations.

faq.question: Does it support RNA-seq and microarray data?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers GEO study searches and file handling for both sequencing and array experiments.

faq.question: Does it perform final statistical interpretation?
faq.answer: No. It can outline analysis steps, but results need statistical and biological review.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: The examples use Python libraries such as GEOparse, Biopython, pandas, scipy, and visualization packages.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys?
faq.answer: Use NCBI API keys only when needed, store them securely, and avoid committing them to shared files.
